To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) the host's ability to carry a tumor burden may be decreased during therapy, (b) the host's decreased ability to carry tumor burden may facilitate MDR emergence, and (c) the host's inability to carry tumor burden is due to damage to the host's ability of nutrient delivery to the tumor.
(1) the emergence of a MDR subpopulation is facilitated when the host environment is damaged, and (2) the facilitation of emergence is greater when the host environment damage is greater.

the presence of a host environment that is damaged by the therapeutic intervention facilitates the emergence of a resistant phenotype in the tumor population, and that this phenomenon is a consequence of a change in the competitive balance between the sensitive and resistant cells in the tumor.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the emergence of MDR cells in a solid mass of cells.
the emergence of MDR cells in a tumor and the impact of therapy upon this phenomenon.
the emergence of MDR cells in a heterogeneous tumor.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the emergence of the MDR phenotype in a solid tumor is a stochastic process that is facilitated in the presence of therapy, but that this facilitation is a consequence of the damage inflicted on the normal host tissues.
MDR emergence may not be a direct consequence of the selection pressure of therapy, but rather an indirect result of host damage caused by therapy.
, in the presence of host impairment, MDR emergence is facilitated by therapy, whereas in the absence of such impairment, the emergence of MDR is delayed by therapy.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the host environment plays an important role in determining the dynamics of the MDR phenotype and that therapy may have an unexpected effect on this phenotype.
, if the host damage is sufficiently large, then the tumor may be able to carry more MDR cells than it can without the damage.
MDR emergence can be facilitated by host damage.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the presence of MDR cells in a population of cells with a wild-type phenotype can be facilitated by the presence of a host with a decreased carrying capacity.
the host response to therapy can be a major determinant of the dynamics of tumor evolution and the emergence of MDR cells in particular, which is a major problem in current cancer treatment.

the presence of MDR cells in a tumor is not necessarily a consequence of therapy but rather a result of the tumor's evolutionary dynamics, and that the tumor's environment can be manipulated to facilitate the emergence of MDR cells.
